title: fix: preserve pending ReplaySSM updates during CPU retraction
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38485.

CPU retraction can lose accepted GDN ReplaySSM updates that remain in a request-indexed replay ring. Backup copies the checkpoint, then reallocation clears the cursor before restore. The restored logical state therefore omits committed updates.

## Modifications

Materialize pending accepted history with the existing all-layer kernel before either CPU backup route. Pass the request row and checkpoint slot separately and preserve residual precision. Empty histories follow the existing copy path; ordinary decoding adds no operation.

## Accuracy Tests

On L4 (prior execution; the six-case test body is unchanged):

- `python3 test/registered/kernel/mem_cache/test_retraction_replayssm_state.py`: all six cases pass; reverting restores the same four failures. Covers wrapped rings, repeated backup, both allocator routes and row reassignment.
- Existing `test_retraction_mamba_backup.py`: both tests pass.
- Real Qwen3.5-0.8B prefill/decode serving with natural KV-pressure retractions: restore errors change from **2/4 to 0/4**, then **3/4** after reversion. All twelve requests complete 80 tokens. Maximum fixed state error is `4.14e-7`; no text-quality improvement is claimed.
- [Fork validation](https://github.com/1sgtpepper/sglang/actions/runs/34265317443) at `e99fdb521552` passes changed-file repository hooks and current-upstream taxonomy checks. The regression is registered in `base-b-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large`; CI verifies the new path is accepted, the old unit path is rejected, and the behavioral fixture is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On the two-layer component fixture, median CPU-backup time is 0.352 ms with no pending history and 0.559 ms with three pending records, using 20 warm samples each. This includes synchronization and copying; it is a comparison of two backup states, not a before/after throughput benchmark.
